summary: A text, code, font or table preview now has a scroll position of its own per file, so it starts at its top (a wide table at its left edge) instead of where the previous file's preview of that kind was left. In preview_body (src/finder/preview.rs) the ID made from the file's path moved from the preview's element, where the kit's scrollbar wrapper replaced it, onto the wrapper itself (.overflow_y_scrollbar().id((..)) and .overflow_scrollbar().id((..))), which is what keys the scroll position, the scrollbar and, on macOS, the bounce. The text of the Text and Code arms sits in an observed div, preview-text, and the table's column is observed as preview-table, so UI tests can see where they are.
changelog: A text, code, font, or table preview could open scrolled to where the previous file's preview was left. After scrolling down in one source file, going back to a file you had already looked at showed it from that place instead of from its first line. It happened in the gallery, the column view, the Preview Pane, and Quick Look. Each file's preview now starts at its top, and a table that is wider than its space starts at its left edge.
behaviour_changes: A text, code, font or table preview no longer opens at the scroll position the previous file's preview of the same kind was left at. Each file's preview starts at its top; a table wider than its space starts at its left edge. Seen wrong before and right after in the gallery (code), the preview pane beside the list (text, font, table) and beside the icons (text), the column view's card (text) and Quick Look's own window (code, text). In Quick Look as the dialog of --term mode it is right after (code); I did not look at it before.
A file's own position is not remembered. Going to another file and coming back starts at the top again, because the position lives only while that file's preview is being drawn.

Unchanged: the file being read keeps its place. Checked for: clicking its row again, frames going by, the mouse moving over it, the preview pane made wider, scrolling further, a quiet reload of the folder, and a change of the preview text size in Quick Look. The place is kept in points, as before, so bigger text shows slightly earlier lines.

The scrollbar's state is per file too. After a scroll in one file, the next file's scrollbar starts hidden instead of staying visible for the rest of its hold. This is from the kit's code (its state is kept under the wrapper's ID), not from a picture.

Unchanged look. 26 pictures of previews shown for the first time are pixel-identical between the trunk's source and the final source once the status bar's free-space text is masked: text, code, JSON, table, font, lines of over 600 characters, an unbroken 400-character token, a one-line file and an empty file; in the gallery, the pane beside the list and beside the icons, the column view's card and Quick Look; light and dark. The end of a file over the 64 KB limit, with its "preview truncated" note, is the same too, apart from the scrollbar thumb, which animates on wall-clock time and differs between two shots of one build.

Element IDs. The scrollbar wrappers are now ("text-preview" | "code-preview" | "font-preview" | "table-preview", path_id(path)), with the kit's (id, "area"), (id, "content"), (id, "scrollbar") and (id, "bounce") under them; before, they were the place in the code where the wrapper is made. New observed IDs for tests: preview-text (Text and Code arms) and preview-table.
Markdown previews, PDFs and explore mode are untouched.
left_out: src/finder/explore.rs, explore mode's view of a single value: the same shape (a per-file ID on the element, the wrapper keyed by where it is made), left alone as the plan of record says. I read the paths and agree that it cannot inherit a position: another file always goes through ExploreState::Loading, which draws the spinner (ensure_explore keeps no cache), and inside one file a single value is only reached from a grid.

No headless test for the font arm: removing its wrapper ID alone fails no test. The repository has no font file, and a test on a system font would be conditional and would need the sample to be taller than the card, which preview-card-height is about to make as tall as the pane. Before/after pictures cover it (preview-scroll-per-file-review-pair-pane-font.png and the implementer's).

docs/manual.md and README.md: neither says where a text, code, font or table preview starts, so nothing became wrong or incomplete. CHANGELOG.md is not edited, as the guide says; the entry is in the commit message.

examples/screenshot.rs has no step that turns the wheel. The pictures used a temporary one that is not committed. It is kept as /home/user/polish-tools/shots/preview-scroll-per-file-scroll-step.patch (the implementer's) and as preview-scroll-per-file-review-add-scroll-steps.py (mine: scroll:x,y,dy[,dx] and, for Quick Look's window, qlscroll:, qlkey: and qlclick:).
cargo clippy --features term was not run: nothing under src/term changed and no signature changed. macOS and Windows were not compiled or run; the change has no platform-specific code.

Not determined: whether, on the trunk, a preview shown for the very first time also inherited the position in the real app. It needs the load to finish before the next frame, and the headless harness always draws a spinner frame first, which drops the position. With the per-file ID it no longer matters.
tests: tests/basics.rs: quick_look_shows_each_file_from_its_first_line (code, Quick Look's own window, arrow keys; also that bigger text leaves the scrolled file where it was)
tests/basics.rs: a_table_preview_starts_at_its_left_edge_however_far_the_last_one_was_scrolled (zip archives, preview pane at its minimum width, sideways wheel)
tests/common/mod.rs: Ui::scroll_point(position, delta); Ui::scroll(id, delta) now calls it with the middle of the element
review_fixes: quick_look_shows_each_file_from_its_first_line now also clicks the bigger-text button on the scrolled file and asserts that it stays where it was. The commit message says that changing the text size keeps the place, and nothing pinned it. It is the other half of what this change is for (a position per file, not per redraw), and the half the next two briefs in this lane can break when they rebuild these scroll areas. It is a guard: green with and without the change. With a wrapper ID that also depends on the text size it fails, 12 against -288.
A why-comment on the observed div around the text in the Text arm, in the words src/finder/nu_panel.rs uses for the same construction. Without it the extra div looks as if it could be removed.
Rebased over search-skeleton-flash and cancel-content-search, which landed meanwhile (no file in common), and ran check.sh again on the result.
notes:
Checked. With the whole src change reverse-applied the three new tests fail, but only for the missing preview-text and preview-table IDs, which come with the change. The proof that counts: with the four wrapper .id((..)) lines taken out and everything else kept, which is the trunk's keying, all three fail at their last assertion (text in the pane: y -222 against 78; code in Quick Look: -288 against 12; table: x 1276 against 1376). Taking out one arm's line at a time fails exactly that arm's test, and the font arm's fails none. check.sh printed CHECK OK on the trunk commit: 461 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures. cargo check --lib -p fffinder (the library as it ships, without test-support) has no warnings.

Throwaway probes, not kept. (1) Where a file's preview is when it is shown again after the next one was scrolled by 300: at its top in the gallery, the column view's card and the pane beside the icons; with the wrapper IDs taken out it is 300 up in the card and in the pane (the gallery I have in pictures), except after a preview of another kind in between, as the brief says. (2) --term mode, Quick Look's dialog over the gallery, both showing the same file: two preview-text elements with different paths; scrolling the dialog's leaves the gallery's alone; stepping to the next file and back shows the first from its top. (3) The file being read keeps its place through everything listed under behaviour_changes. (4) A table preview and the wheel: see below.

Pictures. I took 39 pictures from the trunk's source and the same 39 from the final source, in a folder of my own (preview-scroll-per-file-review-mkpics.py, -shots.sh, -pixdiff.py). The 26 of a preview at rest are pixel-identical. The 7 of a file shown again after the next was scrolled show the other file's position before and the top after: gallery code, pane text light and dark, pane font, pane table (sideways), Quick Look code and text. The 6 taken right after a scroll differ only in the scrollbar thumb's strip, and so do retakes from one build (the thumb's width and fade follow the wall clock).

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt a user, and what the code says. (1) The file being read jumps back to its top, because its key changes from one frame to the next or depends on more than the path: path_id is a SipHash with fixed keys over entry.path and nothing else goes into the ID; the probes and the new assertion in the Quick Look test agree. (2) The extra div around the text changes how it wraps, where the truncated note sits, or an empty file: the pictures at rest are identical, long lines, an unbroken token, the note and an empty file among them. (3) Two previews on screen share or fight over one position or ID. That is possible only in --term mode, where test-support is compiled into the app and Quick Look is a dialog over the browser: the dialog and the gallery have different element paths, keep separate positions, and nothing panics. Split panes are separate views, so their paths differ too. On macOS the kit's bounce is keyed under the wrapper's ID as well; its own documentation asks for the ID to change when the document is replaced (gpui-base-0.8.1/src/scroll_bounce.rs:130), which is what happens now. The tests turn reduced motion on, and with it the bounce takes the same branch on macOS as on Linux, but they have only ever run on Linux.

Found, not fixed (there before this change, outside this brief, and worth a brief of its own): a table preview cannot be scrolled down. Archive listings, and SQLite files and spreadsheets opened through Nushell, show only the rows that fit: 8 of 150 in the preview pane's card and 21 of 150 in Quick Look opened from a 1100 by 700 window, while the manual promises up to 200 items and the footer says "150 items". Headless, a 3724-point-tall table in the pane and in the gallery does not move for a wheel event in points (300) or in lines (5); sideways it moves. The implementer saw the same in pictures. The cause is in how the table arm's scroll area is built: .overflow_scrollbar() (both axes) lays its area out as a flex row (gpui-component-0.8.1/src/scroll/scrollable.rs:176-189), so the content is stretched to the area's height, and GPUI measures what can be scrolled from the area's direct child (gpui-pre-0.3.10/src/elements/div.rs:2035-2062): nothing overflows downward, and the kit's bounce wrapper, which does the vertical scrolling, returns at max <= 0. Ways out: scroll down with .overflow_y_scrollbar() and sideways with a plain overflow_x_scroll inside it, as the list view and explore mode's grid do, or draw the rows with a uniform list as explore mode does. I measured this headlessly and in pictures, not in the app on macOS.

For briefs still to come:
- preview-jump-to-match (next in this lane): the Text and Code arms now end in .overflow_y_scrollbar().id(("text-preview" | "code-preview", path_id)) and the text is inside div().id("preview-text").test_support(). If you replace the wrapper with a scroll area and handles of your own, the reset per file becomes yours to do: a new handle when the previewed path changes, and for nothing else (not a redraw, a text-size change, a quiet reload or a search that runs again). The three tests in tests/basics.rs pin the first part in the pane and in Quick Look's window, and quick_look_shows_each_file_from_its_first_line pins that bigger text leaves the file where it was. They read ui.snapshot("preview-text").bounds().origin, so keep preview-text as something whose top edge moves with the scroll: if the text is split in two for the jump, put it around both parts or on the first. If you wrap your area in ScrollBounce, give it an ID per file too. In --term mode the gallery and Quick Look's dialog both have a preview-text (and would both have a preview-match): look inside the dialog with window.within("dialog"), which I tried. Ui::scroll_point(position, delta) exists; Ui::scroll(id, ..) aims at the middle of the element's unclipped bounds, which for a long text is far outside the preview. In the harness a preview's first load draws a spinner frame, so an inherited position only shows for previews already loaded (select a, select b, scroll b, select a). The font and table arms keep the kit's wrapper; an .id(..) placed before .overflow_*scrollbar() compiles and silently brings this bug back.
- preview-page-keys: its step 4 (keys that scroll a text preview) would rebuild the same four scroll areas, so everything above applies. A table preview has nothing to page through until the bug above is fixed.
- preview-card-height: the three new tests do not depend on the card's 240 points. They turn the wheel 20 points inside the text or table and compare positions. The table test drags the pane to its minimum width (180) so that the table's 300-point minimum width overflows sideways; keep the pane's minimum under that, or its "b.zip scrolled" assertion fails. Your plan says table previews keep scrolling inside the box: sideways only, see above.
- stale-previews-and-cancel: a preview replaced in place for the same path (your "keep the old value until the new one lands") keeps its scroll position, cut to the new length; a spinner frame, as after forget_previews, starts it at the top. That was so before this change too. If a reread file should start at its top, that needs a reset of its own.
- tab-bar-overflow, results-scroll-reset: Ui::scroll(id, delta) keeps its signature and what it does; only the label the hang watchdog prints now names the position, not the ID. Ui::scroll_point sits right after it in tests/common/mod.rs.
- quick-look-empty-state, quick-look-window-mixup, image-preview-details, thumbnail-memory: they touch src/finder/preview.rs or Quick Look but not these four arms; expect at most a textual conflict near preview_body.
